blocks.value: A method is a collection of statements grouped together to perform an operation. The void keyword means a method doesn't return a value.

A parameter is a variable listed in a method's declaration; an argument is the actual value passed in when the method is called. The value returned must match the method's declared return type: you can't return an int from a method declared to return boolean.

Instance variables are declared outside any method, constructor, or block; they belong to the object itself. Local variables are declared inside a method and only exist there; nothing outside that method can see them.
this refers to the object that the method was called on. It's useful for referring to an instance variable when a parameter or local variable happens to share its name.
